classification.classification_note: The immediate fault is a write through the first nested CK_ATTRIBUTE's destination pointer. Vulnerable nested-array decoding allocates raw bytes for the outer attribute value but never initializes or allocates the inner CK_ATTRIBUTE.pValue fields before the nested serializer writes through them.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the rpc-server where parsing CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE allows nested attribute arrays. The current internal API cannot determine the actual size of data that needs to be stored, as ulValueLen is set to the attribute count times sizeof(CK_ATTRIBUTE), leading to potential issues with memory allocation.
bug_description.normalized: In p11-kit's RPC server, a C_CreateObject request can carry a top-level template attribute whose type has CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE set, such as CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE. proto_read_attribute_array() first probes that attribute with pValue == NULL, so p11_rpc_buffer_get_attribute_array_value() can only walk the nested structure and recover a flat CK_ATTRIBUTE-array shape. Vulnerable server code does not reject that CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE after the probe; it allocates raw attrs[i].pValue bytes for the outer value and then re-decodes the nested attribute array directly into that raw buffer as if it were an initialized CK_ATTRIBUTE[]. p11_rpc_message_alloc_extra() fills fresh allocations with 0xff, so the first nested CK_ATTRIBUTE starts with pValue = 0xffffffffffffffff. In the staged witness, the nested attribute header is CKA_COLOR, so p11_rpc_buffer_get_byte_value() writes one byte through that invalid pointer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer reports a SEGV write at p11-kit/rpc-message.c:1080. The fix adds an early temp.type & CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE rejection in proto_read_attribute_array().

source.description: First project parser step inside the vulnerable CreateObject template decoder: it reads the top-level CK_ATTRIBUTE array count from the attacker-controlled RPC request body.
source.value_from: The staged 46-byte `poc` is a p11-kit RPC request with call id 20 (`C_CreateObject`) and signature `"uaA"`. After the 8-byte session field, the next four bytes are `00 20 20 20`, which this statement materializes as `n_attrs = 0x00202020`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first template attribute header comes straight from the RPC bytes. In the staged witness, these fields decode as `type = 0x40000211 (CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE)`, `validity = 0x20`, and `length = 0x20202020`, which together steer the unsupported nested-attribute-array decode and the later raw-value allocation.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable server never rejects a probed template element whose `temp.type` has `CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE` set before entering this branch. It therefore allocates a flat `attrs[i].pValue` buffer for an unsupported nested attribute array and prepares to re-decode it as an ordinary value.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch inserts `if (temp.type & CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE) { ... return PARSE_ERROR; }` immediately after the first `p11_rpc_buffer_get_attribute()` probe and before this allocation path.

sink.description: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer crash site. The nested CKA_COLOR byte decoder writes one byte through `value`, which is the first nested CK_ATTRIBUTE's uninitialized `pValue` field.
sink.note: The saved Stage 01 trace reports `SEGV on unknown address 0xffffffffffffffff` caused by a WRITE in this statement, reached through `p11_rpc_buffer_get_attribute -> p11_rpc_buffer_get_attribute_array_value -> p11_rpc_buffer_get_attribute -> proto_read_attribute_array -> rpc_C_CreateObject`.

parser_admitted.description: The RPC header has already parsed as `call_id = 20` with request signature `"uaA"`, so `p11_rpc_server_handle()` dispatches into `rpc_C_CreateObject()`, whose `IN_ATTRIBUTE_ARRAY(template, count)` macro enters the vulnerable `proto_read_attribute_array()` path.

fine_trace.note: Reads the top-level template count from the attacker-controlled `uaA` request body. In the staged witness those bytes are `00 20 20 20`, so `n_attrs = 0x00202020`; because the count is nonzero, the loop at line 308 enters its first iteration and reaches the attacker-controlled attribute header.

The first template element's header is materialized from the RPC bytes as `type = 0x40000211 (CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE)`, `validity = 0x20` (true), and declared `length = 0x20202020`. Because the type carries `CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE`, the decoder will treat the following bytes as a nested CK_ATTRIBUTE array.

During the first probe of the outer CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE, `attr->pValue` is NULL, so the attribute-array decoder has no backing storage for nested values. It reads `count = 1`, reuses a single stack `temp` slot while walking that one nested attribute, and reports only the structural size `1 * sizeof(CK_ATTRIBUTE) = 24`.

After the probe returns, the decoder discards the computed structural size `24` and overwrites `attr->ulValueLen` with the attacker-declared outer length `0x20202020`, checking only that `24 <= length`. The probed outer attribute therefore propagates as `temp.type = CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE`, `temp.ulValueLen = 0x20202020`.

No `temp.type & CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE` guard rejects the probed CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE here. Because `temp.ulValueLen != -1`, control enters this branch and allocates a flat outer-value buffer for an unsupported nested attribute array.

The newly allocated outer-value buffer is deliberately filled with `0xff`. When the second decode later reinterprets the returned region as the first nested CK_ATTRIBUTE record, that inner record starts with `pValue = 0xffffffffffffffff` and `ulValueLen = -1`.

On the second decode of the same outer attribute, `value` is the newly allocated `attrs[i].pValue`, so the decoder aliases that raw buffer as `CK_ATTRIBUTE *attr` and passes the first nested slot into `p11_rpc_buffer_get_attribute()`.

The first nested attribute header in the witness decodes as `type = 0x405 (CKA_COLOR)`, so `map_attribute_to_value_type()` selects the byte-value serializer and invokes it with the current inner destination pointer `attr->pValue`. Because the slot came from the 0xff-filled buffer in step 6, that pointer is still `0xffffffffffffffff`.

Sink. The byte-value decoder stores one byte of the nested CKA_COLOR value through `value = attr->pValue = 0xffffffffffffffff`, producing the saved UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer `SEGV on unknown address 0xffffffffffffffff` caused by a WRITE at this line.

format.name: p11-kit PKCS#11 RPC request
format.contract: The staged `poc` is the exact 46-byte big-endian p11-kit RPC request blob. It encodes `call_id = 0x14 (P11_RPC_CALL_C_CreateObject)` and signature `"uaA"`, followed by an 8-byte session value, a top-level template count field `00 20 20 20`, and a first template attribute header `40 00 02 11 20 20 20 20 20` (`type = CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE`, nonzero validity, declared length `0x20202020`). That outer attribute's value bytes begin with nested count `00 00 00 01` and then one valid nested attribute header `00 00 04 05 20 20 20 20 20`, which decodes as `type = CKA_COLOR`, nonzero validity, declared length `0x20202020`, followed by the one-byte payload `20`. Those exact witness semantics make the server re-decode a `CKF_ARRAY_ATTRIBUTE` element into raw CK_ATTRIBUTE storage and reproduce the saved invalid-pointer write.
